newsitem.title: USA: Retail stocks rise on higher January sales.
newsitem.headline: Retail stocks rise on higher January sales.

text.p: Most retail stocks traded steady to higher on Thursday after they reported January comparable-store sales, boosted by continued strength in apparel, near or better than expectations.
Computer and consumer electronic retailers, however, continued to show slow sales, analysts said.
The Salomon Brothers same-store sales growth index registered a 7.2 percent gain for the month, compared with a 1.7 percent rise a year ago. December's index showed a 6.1 percent gain.

Apparel continued to lead the way in sales, analysts said, with chain stores such as Limited Inc, Spiegel Inc, including its Eddie Bauer unit, Gap Inc and many key department stores posting higher sales.
"The numbers were pretty good," said Karen Sack, a retail analyst for Standard & Poor's. "Having said that, January is a mark-down month. That means margins aren't really good."
Shares of Gap traded 7/8 higher at 30-3/4, Limited rose 1/8 to 17-1/4, Spiegel was up 1/4 at seven, and Gymboree Corp rose 1/4 to 22.

Shares of the largest U.S. retailer, Wal-Mart Stores Inc, were up 3/8 at 23-5/8 and Kmart Corp traded up 3/8 at 11. Sears, Roebuck and Co rose 1-1/4 to 49-3/4 after reporting double-digit growth in its full-line stores sales, and J C Penney Co Inc was unchanged at 47 after it climbed 3/8 to 47-3/8 ealier on Thursday.

Consumer electronics retailer Best Buy Co Inc posted a larger-than-expected 15 percent January same-store sales decline and its shares lost 1/2 to trade at 9-1/8. Circuit City Stores Inc's Circuit City Group same-store sales fell 11 percent, close to estimates, and its stock was up 3/8 at 35-1/4.

"Consumer electronics and home office continue to perform sluggishly in an extremely competitive environment, and also facing sluggish demand," said Saul Yaari, an analyst for Piper Jaffrey, adding he had expected a 10 percent decline for both Best Buy and Circuit City.
